applicable_when: The kernel processes a 2048x25 = 51,200 element layout permutation (convolution weight reformat). With XBLOCK=128 and xnumel=25, only 25 of 128 threads per block do real work — 80% of threads are masked idle. This produces a grid of only 256 blocks across 132 SMs (0.12 waves), causing catastrophically low occupancy (10.9%). The fix is to use @triton.autotune to explore tile configurations where XBLOCK is sized closer to xnumel (e.g., 32) and YBLOCK is increased (e.g., 32 or 64) to pack more work per block and improve SM utilization.
